newsitem.title: USA: Standard Financial holder calls suit meritless.
newsitem.headline: Standard Financial holder calls suit meritless.

text.p: LaSalle/Kross Partners LP, which owns 5.4 percent of Standard Financial Inc, said Wednesday a lawsuit filed against it by the thrift was without merit.

The suit, filed in federal court in Chicago, alleges that the investment fund falsely stated in an SEC filing that it had acquired its stake in Standard Financial for investment purposes, Standard Financial general counsel Randall Schwartz said Tuesday.
"We don't believe it has any merit," LaSalle/Kross principal Richard Nelson said in an interview Wednesday. "The lawsuit appears to be harassment and intimidation."

Nelson said LaSalle/Kross will continue in its efforts to have two directors elected to the Standard Financial board. He also said a meeting with Standard Financial's management was "not very fruitful" and did not change LaSalle/Kross's opinion that Standard Financial was an underperforming company.
Standard Financial shares were down 3/16 at 21-1/16.
